messages:
evan: sec-bot fired an alert — ptrace syscalls observed from pod prod/web-78-5f9c7d (node: ip-10-2-3-45). tagging here so oncall can triage quickly.
sec-bot: [ALERT][sev=high] unusual ptrace/syscall tracing observed inside container image=redwood/web:1.4.2, process pid=2431, cmdline="/app/start.sh". Noted open /proc/kcore and suid binary access.
julia: acknowledged. I'm on it, pulling logs and node metrics. first step: isolate pod and snapshot node.
angela: if ptrace is active inside container that can indicate userns/ptrace escape attempts or a malicious debug binary. prioritize containment.
evan: suggested containment checklist: 1) scale down or delete pod, 2) cordon node, 3) capture memory and /proc, 4) collect audit logs, 5) check RBAC and service account tokens.
omar: i'll cordon node ip-10-2-3-45 now and start an ephemeral host for artifact collection.
omar: commands I ran:```sh
kubectl cordon ip-10-2-3-45
kubectl get pods -o wide | grep ip-10-2-3-45
kubectl delete pod web-78-5f9c7d --namespace=prod --grace-period=0 --force
```
leo: captured kubelet journal and containerd events. grabbing crictl ps and `ctr tasks list` to see other processes.
leo: snippet from containerd log: "containerd: start exec id=ae3f... pid=2431 cmd=/bin/sh -c ./dbg; ptrace_attach detected"
julia: logs show process spawned via /tmp/.Xc4 and a binary named "dbg" with suid bit set. image manifest digest matches known digest, but the image tarball extracted from node has an extra layer with changed file perms — suspicious.
tara: any KMS access anomalies? if data plane keys were accessed we need to rotate and notify compliance.
evan: good call — audit KMS logs now. I see a spike in decrypt requests for projects/redwood-prod/keys/customer-data at 1954320900 — client_id=web-78-5f9c7d. that's within ~100s of the alert.
dena: flagging for potential data-access incident. compliance wants timeline and whether any exported blobs left the cluster.
angela: also check for new ClusterRoleBindings or serviceaccount tokens created recently. run:```sh
kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o wide --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 20
kubectl get rolebinding -A --field-selector metadata.creationTimestamp>="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
```
evan: ran a quick check — found a RoleBinding in prod namespace bound to sa:debug-helper created 2025-08-14T02:11:03Z, grants edit. unclear who created it.
julia: cross-reference with audit logs: apiserver logs show a request from ip 34.75.120.9 using token from serviceaccount debug-helper at 2025-08-14T02:10:50Z to create the rolebinding. token was valid.
leo: looking at kube-apiserver audit logs: userAgent:"kubelet/v1.25" which is odd for a user-created request. suspect compromised node or leaked token.
omar: node was already cordoned. i'm taking a disk snapshot and will spin up the node in isolated network for forensic work. please avoid restarting workloads on other nodes until we confirm no image tamper.
angela: note — image digest in registry matches manifest, but node-local overlayfs shows an additional layer with modified mode bits. could be post-deploy tampering. check imagePullPolicy and admission webhooks.
julia: pulling registry object store keys for image layers now and will compare checksums.
evan: immediate actions agreed: (1) cordoned node (done), (2) deleted suspect pod (done), (3) rotate KMS key access token/credentials for customer-data key, (4) revoke any serviceaccount tokens for debug-helper and related SAs, (5) enable higher-fidelity audit logging for apiserver and kubelet for 72h, (6) escalate to incidents channel and legal.
tara: please open an incident ticket with severity and timeline — i'll draft comms for customers if needed.
dena: legal: preserve logs and evidence chain. avoid altering node images; use snapshots. we may need to notify customers if exfiltration confirmed.
leo: collected artifacts: /var/log/containers/web-78-5f9c7d.log (attached to internal store), /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/extra-layer.tar (hash: sha256:ab3f...), memory dump compressed (path: s3://forensics-snapshots/1954321000/memdump.gz).
julia: comparing layer hash to registry: registry layer hash is sha256:7c9d... not equal to ab3f... => confirms node-local modification.
angela: search for cronjobs or DaemonSets that could have mutated images post-pull. run:```sh
kubectl get daemonset -A -o yaml | yq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, ns:.metadata.namespace, image:.spec.template.spec.containers[].image}'
```
omar: found a daemonset 'node-tools' in kube-system with image registry.internal/tools:latest created by infra-ops 2024-11-02 — it shouldn't have permissions to write overlayfs but it's running privileged: true. that is a change since last audit. marking as suspect.
evan: big red flag: privileged daemonset that can write host overlay + ptrace observed. we need to revoke that daemonset and audit who pushed that image tag.
leo: checked ECR push logs — tools:latest was pushed from CI runner ip 35.201.12.4 using deploy-bot token. was the token rotated?
julia: deploy-bot token last rotated 2024-12-01. CI job logs show a manual trigger on 2025-08-13 23:58 UTC. owner is infra-ops@redwood.
tara: loop in infra-ops and CI team. also verify CI job environment for leaked secrets.
dena: compliance: require list of all S3/KMS objects accessed in window 1954320800-1954321200. we need that for DPI assessment.
evan: plan (24h): full node forensic, rotate KMS access keys and revoke implicated serviceaccount tokens, remove privileged node-tools daemonset, rotate deploy-bot token, audit CI runners and infra-ops accounts, and prepare customer impact assessment.
angela: add host-level detection rules: alert on ptrace syscalls inside containers, and detect overlayfs layer additions with unexpected mode changes.
omar: creating perms change PR to disallow privileged DaemonSets without explicit approval. linking policy PR: https://git.internal/redwood/policies/pull/422
julia: I'm dumping apiserver audit logs slice and handing to forensics. also creating replayable kubectl commands for reproducing the timeline.
leo: tagging evidence with hash manifest and storing to evidence bucket with immutability flag.
evan: moving this thread to #incidents and will update there. thanks everyone — next sync in 30m. :lock: 
sec-bot: Incident escalated to incident-manager. incident_id=INC-2025-215. artifacts: [/var/log/containers/web-78-5f9c7d.log, memdump.gz, extra-layer.tar].
